page: Amazon Web Services r8id.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features 192 vCPUs derived from 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running up to 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware acceleration instructions include AVX-512 extensions and AMX tile and int8 matrices. The instance is outfitted with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of 11,400 GB across NVMe SSD instance volumes, supported by 75 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark outcomes show top-tier multi-threaded compute and in-memory operations. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 207,544.02, while PassMark multi-core and database operational tests placed within the top 10%. Memory read bandwidth achieved 573.59 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks and 15,323.26 GB/sec for small cached blocks. Redis SET operations measured 245.08 million operations per second, complemented by a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 1,202.39 GB/sec and static web serving throughput of 271.94 GB/sec.

Single-core performance presents a moderate profile relative to its parallel scale, with stress-ng single-core achieving an average 2,119.29 and Geekbench single-core reporting 2,175.0. Although lacking dedicated GPU hardware, AMX matrix acceleration enables capable CPU-driven language model inference, reaching 44.98 tokens per second on 7B model generation. With extensive DDR5 capacity and fast local NVMe volumes, the instance provides high resource density for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory caching like Redis, distributed data analytics, and real-time transaction processing systems.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.48xlarge is a high-density, memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor reaching 3.9 GHz, alongside 1536.0 GB of DDR5 system memory and 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. While single-thread execution rates remain average, multi-threaded metrics rank in the top 10%, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 207,544.02 and Redis throughput reaching 245.08 million operations per second. Hardware includes 75 Gbps baseline networking, AVX-512, and AMX acceleration without discrete GPUs. The r8id.48xlarge is built for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching platforms, and data-intensive transaction workloads requiring substantial RAM and local storage bandwidth.
